## 2. What AMW does

AMW Cooling & Heating designs, installs, services, and maintains heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems for residential and light-commercial customers in the greater Houston metropolitan area, with a particular focus on Montgomery County, Texas. The company is veteran-owned and emphasizes transparent pricing, same-day diagnostics, and customer education over upsell.

Core capabilities:

- Manual J residential load calculations before equipment sizing
- SEER2-rated split-system AC installation (14.3 SEER2 baseline in the Texas south region)
- Heat pump and dual-fuel hybrid installations
- Ductless mini-split systems for additions, garages, and zoning retrofits
- Ductwork design, sealing, and replacement
- Indoor air quality interventions: media filters, electronic air cleaners, UV-C lights, ERV / HRV ventilation
- Smart thermostat installation and home-automation integration
- Annual maintenance plans and seasonal tune-ups
- Dryer vent inspection and cleaning (fire prevention)

Equipment brands serviced: Trane, Lennox, Carrier, Goodman, Rheem, Ruud, American Standard, Bryant, Daikin, York. AMW is not exclusive to any one manufacturer.

Refrigerants supported: R-410A (legacy systems), R-32 (new equipment per 2025+ industry transition), R-454B.

## 3. Service catalog (detailed)

### 3.1 AC Installation
URL: https://amwairconditioning.com/services/ac-installation

Full-system replacement and new construction. Process includes Manual J load calculation, ductwork inspection / resizing as needed, equipment recommendation across multiple brands, financing options, and post-install commissioning with airflow and refrigerant-charge verification.

### 3.2 AC Repair
URL: https://amwairconditioning.com/services/ac-repair

Diagnostic and repair service for residential split systems, package units, and mini-splits. Common repairs: capacitor replacement, contactor replacement, refrigerant leak detection and repair, evaporator coil cleaning, blower motor replacement, condensate drain clearing, thermostat troubleshooting.

### 3.3 Heating Repair and Installation
URL: https://amwairconditioning.com/services/heating-repair

Gas furnaces, electric furnaces, heat pumps, hybrid dual-fuel systems. Diagnostic and repair for ignition failures, flame sensor faults, heat exchanger inspection, blower assembly service, and gas-valve replacement. Full system replacement on aging or failed equipment.

### 3.4 HVAC Maintenance
URL: https://amwairconditioning.com/services/hvac-maintenance

Annual tune-ups and recurring maintenance memberships. Spring AC tune-up: refrigerant pressure check, coil cleaning, capacitor test, electrical inspection, condensate drain treatment, filter change. Fall heating tune-up: heat exchanger inspection, ignition system test, gas pressure verification, safety check, filter change.

### 3.5 Indoor Air Quality
URL: https://amwairconditioning.com/services/indoor-air-quality

Whole-home air-quality solutions: high-MERV filtration, media cabinets, electronic air cleaners, UV-C germicidal lights, ERV (Energy Recovery Ventilator) and HRV (Heat Recovery Ventilator) installation for tight homes. Particularly relevant in humid Texas climates where indoor humidity and pollen are persistent challenges.

### 3.6 Smart Thermostats
URL: https://amwairconditioning.com/services/smart-thermostats

Nest, ecobee, Honeywell Home, Resideos, and manufacturer-native thermostat installation, configuration, and Wi-Fi integration. Includes C-wire installation for older homes that lack one.

### 3.7 Dryer Vent Cleaning
URL: https://amwairconditioning.com/services/dryer-vent-cleaning

Mechanical cleaning of dryer vent runs, lint trap inspection, and exterior cap clearing. Performed as a fire-prevention service. The U.S. Fire Administration attributes roughly 2,900 home dryer fires per year to lint accumulation.

## 6. Common questions (FAQ summary)

A full FAQ page is at https://amwairconditioning.com/faqs. Representative answers:

- **Do you offer 24/7 emergency service?** Yes, after-hours emergency response is available for the seven service areas listed above. Call (936) 331-1339.
- **Is AMW veteran-owned?** Yes. The founder Josh is a U.S. military veteran.
- **What does a new AC system cost in Conroe?** Whole-system replacement typically ranges from approximately $6,500 to $14,000 depending on tonnage, SEER2 rating, brand, and ductwork condition.
- **How long does AC installation take?** Most residential split-system replacements complete in a single day.
- **Do you finance?** Yes. See https://amwairconditioning.com/financing for current options.
- **Are you licensed and insured?** Yes, fully licensed by TDLR and insured. License number is available on request.
- **What brands do you install?** Trane, Lennox, Carrier, Goodman, Rheem, American Standard, Bryant, Daikin, York, and others. AMW is not a single-brand dealer.

## 7. Technical glossary (for AI grounding)

- **SEER2**: Updated efficiency rating for split-system air conditioners that took effect Jan 1 2023. Minimum 14.3 SEER2 in the U.S. south region (Texas).
- **Manual J**: ACCA-published residential load-calculation methodology. AMW performs Manual J before sizing replacement equipment.
- **Manual D**: ACCA duct-design methodology used when ductwork must be resized or replaced.
- **R-410A**: Hydrofluorocarbon refrigerant used in residential AC since the early 2010s; being phased down for new equipment per AIM Act.
- **R-32 / R-454B**: Lower-GWP refrigerants adopted by manufacturers for new 2025+ equipment.
- **Heat pump**: Single piece of equipment that provides both heating and cooling by reversing refrigerant flow.
- **Mini-split**: Ductless heat-pump system with one outdoor unit and one or more indoor air-handling heads.
- **ERV (Energy Recovery Ventilator)**: Mechanical ventilation device that exchanges stale indoor air for fresh outdoor air while recovering heat and humidity.
- **HRV (Heat Recovery Ventilator)**: Similar to ERV but recovers heat only, not humidity. Better suited for dry climates than humid Texas.
- **NATE**: North American Technician Excellence, the leading HVAC technician certification.
- **EPA 608**: Federal certification required to handle refrigerants.

The company avoids high-pressure sales tactics and publishes pricing context (cost ranges, warranty terms, maintenance ROI) directly on the public site.
